guest.bio_context: Calum Scott is a singer-songwriter from Hull who rose to fame after receiving the golden buzzer on Britain's Got Talent. Before his music career, he worked for Hull City Council. He has released three studio albums, the latest being 'Avanoir', and has collaborated with artists including Lost Frequencies, Ronan Keating, and the Whitney Houston estate. He performed at King Charles III's coronation and at Wembley Arena.

pending_qa.q: What is Calum Scott's third album and how has it changed his career?
pending_qa.r: Calum Scott's third album is called 'Avanoir', released in October of the previous year. He says it has 'completely changed his life', allowing him to write more diverse and upbeat songs such as 'Roots', 'At Your Worst', and 'Lighthouse', and has led to bigger shows, festival headline bookings, and a new sense of creative confidence.

pending_qa.q: How did Calum Scott deal with imposter syndrome as a musician from Hull?
pending_qa.r: Calum Scott says he always had imposter syndrome as 'a lad from Hull', with a voice in the back of his mind saying 'it's only a matter of time before this all goes away.' Writing his third album helped silence that voice and allowed him to feel 'more confident and more content than I ever have.'

pending_qa.q: What mental health struggles has Calum Scott openly discussed?
pending_qa.r: Calum Scott has spoken openly about body dysmorphia, suicidal thoughts, and periods of being 'very, very cruel' to himself. He credits his mother Debs as 'the core anchor as to why I'm still here' and says therapy 'hands down saved my life' by helping him reinforce positive self-talk and build mental resilience.

pending_qa.q: How did therapy help Calum Scott manage his mental health?
pending_qa.r: Calum Scott described therapy exercises such as looking in a mirror and repeating 'I am enough' five or ten times, which he initially felt 'stupid' doing. He came to understand that just as negative self-talk repeated enough times becomes believed, the same principle applies to positive reinforcement, and therapy helped him build 'a strong and unwavering support' mentally.

pending_qa.q: What did Calum Scott say about his song 'Bridges' and its impact compared to streaming numbers?
pending_qa.r: Calum Scott wrote 'Bridges' about a moment when he was on a bridge and felt like throwing his life away. Despite having significantly fewer streams than his collaboration 'Where Are You Now?' (1.7 billion streams), he considers 'Bridges' more meaningful because people have told him it made them 'feel seen and heard' during their darkest moments.

pending_qa.q: What was the streaming success of Calum Scott's collaboration with Lost Frequencies on 'Where Are You Now?'
pending_qa.r: The Lost Frequencies track 'Where Are You Now?' featuring Calum Scott reached 1.7 billion streams. Calum described it as a slow build, noting he worked the record for about two years — it underperformed in its first year, then climbed back to reach number one on the Top 40 in its second year.

pending_qa.q: Why does Calum Scott consider it important to remain based in Hull despite his international success?
pending_qa.r: Calum Scott says Hull is where he was born, raised, and where all his family live, and that staying grounded there is essential to remaining 'just Callum' between tours. He frames it explicitly: 'Callum Scott goes all around the world, but Callum's heart belongs in Hull.' He also cites the importance of supporting local charities and businesses in his home city.

pending_qa.q: What is Calum Scott's view on social media metrics and self-worth?
pending_qa.r: Calum Scott is critical of equating social media metrics with personal or artistic value. He pointed out that before his Britain's Got Talent audition, a Facebook post announcing his audition received only three likes — one from his mother — while after the audition aired it received 10,000 likes. He argues this shows you 'can go from zero to hero with one post' and that talent and authenticity matter more than follower counts.

pending_qa.q: What role did Calum Scott play on The Voice Germany and how did it affect his profile there?
pending_qa.r: Calum Scott served as a coach on The Voice Germany. He credits this role with helping his music 'blow up' in Germany, where he has performed at festivals including one in the city of Balingen and says he has 'a lot of love for Germany.'
